request.questionText: Buildings that invest in energy efficiency reduce global-warming greenhouse gas emissions and costs associated with energy consumption. Sustainability may also be appealing to building tenants. Do “green-certified” buildings offer a premium on the commercial real-estate market? An analyst at an architecture firm uses data on 7,894 commercial buildings to fit a model predicting revenue per square foot by whether the building has a green rating, producing the following results: lm(rev_psf ~ green_rating, data=greenbuildings) %>% get_regression_table(digits=1) %>% select(-std_error:-p_value) Next, they fit the model with an additional predictor variable for building age in years: lm(rev_psf ~ green_rating + age, data=greenbuildings) %>% get_regression_table(digits=1) %>% select(-std_error:-p_value) Which of the following statements is accurate with respect to the results of these two regression models? (1) Both models suggest (with 95% confidence) that a green rating is associated with an increase in revenue. (2) The second model's green rating coefficient suggests that some of the green rating effect observed with the first model was, in fact, partially attributable to variation in building age. (3) The first model estimates an overall relationship between green rating and revenue.
